instruction: Add the Steinberg et al. (2003) cocoa flavonoids paper to the reference list as the 14th entry, and insert '[14]' in the fourth paragraph where '<add here>' is marked.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the docx file from the container using python-docx and splits document into body and references sections.
Metric correctly awards 0.5 for Steinberg present in the document and 0.5 for '[14]' in body text with '<add here>' absent, matching the two sub-goals.

The '<add here>' removal check plus '[14]' presence provides a reasonable proxy for verifying the citation was inserted at the correct location in the fourth paragraph, since there is only one '<add here>' marker.

Missing positional check: the instruction requires Steinberg as the '14th entry', but the getter only checks presence of 'Steinberg' anywhere in the doc. Adding Steinberg as entry #3 or #20 would still return has_steinberg=True.

has_steinberg checks both refs_text and body_text — a casual mention of 'Steinberg' in the essay body (without adding the reference entry) would incorrectly satisfy the check. Restricting to refs_text only would be more accurate.
No explicit check that '[14]' is specifically in the fourth paragraph; only that it appears somewhere in body text. In practice this is mitigated because '<add here>' was in a single location.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add a positional check: parse the references section, enumerate numbered entries, and verify that the entry containing 'Steinberg' is at index 14 (or labeled '[14]').
Restrict has_steinberg to check refs_text only, not body_text, to ensure the reference was actually added to the reference list.
Optionally, identify which paragraph number the '[14]' appears in and verify it is the fourth paragraph of the body to fully satisfy the instruction.
